primary_task: Review (or write) a Cloudflare Worker's code and configuration against Workers best practices and flag the listed anti-patterns, validating with the project's existing type-check and runtime tests.

requirements.name: developers.cloudflare.com
requirements.evidence: Retrieve relevant Cloudflare documentation to verify API, configuration, runtime behavior, and limit claims. ... For missing evidence, consult [Workers best practices](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/best-practices/workers-best-practices/) or find the affected product in the [Cloudflare docs directory](https://developers.cloudflare.com/directory/).
requirements.basis: egress_deny: "*.cloudflare.com"; lacks: "network access to hosts outside the egress allow-list: ... other hosts are refused, for example huggingface.co, Microsoft Learn and Azure endpoints, Cloudflare, Expo, Neon and NVIDIA"

requirements.name: wrangler
requirements.evidence: Use the installed Wrangler schema for config fields. ... generate binding types with `wrangler types`.
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, ...)"; egress_allow: "registry.npmjs.org"

requirements.name: project type-checker and runtime test runner (e.g. tsc, vitest)
requirements.evidence: Use the project's existing checks for affected Workers behavior: type-check binding or handler contract changes, and run relevant runtime tests for behavior changes.
requirements.basis: tools.bash: "install packages from the open registries (pip from PyPI, npm, ...), build, test, run CLIs and scripts"

requirements.name: read/edit (project source and wrangler config)
requirements.evidence: Use the project's installed versions, generated types, and Wrangler compatibility settings as the baseline for existing code.
requirements.basis: tools.read: "read files in the working directory; search them by name pattern or content (glob, grep)"

notes: Reading taken: retrieval of Cloudflare docs is a preference ("Prefer retrieval over pre-training") and the explicit doc links are for "missing evidence", so the review can be done from the project's installed types, Wrangler schema and code; the egress is marked not hard. Under the stricter reading that "Retrieve relevant Cloudflare documentation to verify API, configuration, runtime behavior, and limit claims" is a mandatory step, egress:developers.cloudflare.com is hard and unavailable and the verdict would be BLOCKED (web_search snippets or the cloudflare-docs GitHub repo could be a workaround the document does not name). Reference files (references/configuration.md etc.) are part of the skill bundle; their presence is unknown and they are read only 'relevant to the task'. No Cloudflare account is needed for review; deploying is not part of the task.
